main_issue: Who deals with the unwashed pork pan tonight, and whether the household agrees to a rule of washing the pan (and cleaning up generally) right after use.

A-B.evidence: A denies use (T1), B 'Me neither' (T2); later both accept the wash-right-after rule (T13 A 'Yes', T16 B 'Yeah, fine'), but they never address each other.

A-C.evidence: C says the user should sort it out (T9); A says 'it wasn't me' (T11) but agrees to the rule (T13); C agrees (T18) and extends it to cleaning up after oneself.

A-D.evidence: A asks D about the special cleaning (T5, T7), then says 'Fine, washing up straight away is a good idea' (T11) and 'Yes' (T13) to D's rule.

B-C.evidence: B only says 'Me neither' (T2) and 'Yeah, fine' (T16); C accepts the rule (T18). They share the rule but never interact.

B-D.evidence: D asks B directly (T14); B answers 'Yeah, fine' (T16), accepting D's proposed rule.

C-D.evidence: C wanted the user to fix it (T9) while D takes the cleaning on this time (T10); C then says 'Yes. And not just the pan...' (T18), endorsing the rule with a broader scope.
